verdict: Under the accepted circular-security assumption, the current sigma128 lvl1 family misses the strict >=128-bit classical screen: 129.6479 BDGL16 and127.7888 MATZOV. This is borderline approximately128-bit estimated strength, not a practical break. Recommend sigma256 (135.1866/133.0916 bits) across the lvl1 family, followed by regeneration and correctness qualification. No runtime noise parameters were changed by this assessment.

assumptions.circular_security: Accepted for the complete evaluation-key graph per user instruction; not treated as an outstanding parameter-screen blocker.
assumptions.CSPRNG: Current BLAKE3 generation is assumed cryptographic. Historical SplitMix v1 material is not rehabilitated.
assumptions.noise: Variance-matched DiscreteGaussian proxy for ideal truncated continuous normals. Not an exact finite-precision PMF theorem.
assumptions.models: Pinned classical BDGL16 and MATZOV, beta search cap4096; no quantum-security claim.

known_zero_sample_derivation.equation: For a PKS body row: b(X)=a(X)*t(X)+c+e(X), where c depends on source secret and gadget but is a constant polynomial. Extract coefficient1 to get b_1=<SE_1(a),t>+e_1.
known_zero_sample_derivation.public_operation: SampleExtractIndex uses only the public ciphertext; no source or destination secret is needed to extract this known-zero equation.
known_zero_sample_derivation.mask_law: SE_1 is a signed permutation of the uniform mask coefficients; selecting one fixed coordinate per independently encrypted row yields independent scalar masks, rather than counting correlated rotations as independent.
known_zero_sample_derivation.finite_sample_result: With m65568 the minimum equals the unbounded screen. The reported dual-hybrid optimum uses m1024. The existing independent rows already suffice.
known_zero_sample_derivation.arithmetic_caveat: Ideal TRLWE encryption gives exactly the stated noise law. Independent schoolbook checks on the current FFT backend observed zero multiplication-rounding errors on131072 audited coefficients; this is an empirical implementation check, not a universal rounding proof.

combined_estimates.scope: Classical generic LWE cost estimates for variance-matched discrete-Gaussian proxies. Circular security accepted; no quantum or exact-sampler/ring-specific proof.

run_provenance.note: Initial run screened four attacks at interior grid points. The subsequent30-result extension completed all seven attacks there. The final reproduction script requests the combined166 results directly; two additional nominal-RMS controls are below.

import sys,json

 name,_,attack,result=a.estimate((Path('/mnt/selection'),'nominal_sigma128',profile,model,'dual_hybrid'))

results.source: synthetic keys only; independent schoolbook integer phase audit

sampler_and_implementation_probe.method: Synthetic keys only; independent O(n^2) integer negacyclic phase oracle. 65536 coefficients each at sigma128 and256. Twenty small-domain PKS rows demonstrate known-zero extraction and target-noise selection.

retune_requirements: Use sigma256 at the lvl1 target (normalized alpha2^-24), including fresh TLWE/TRLWE encryption, BR-key rows, private-switch rows and legacy/direct output material. Updating only the ring key does not address the weak family.
Do not override only PKS::alpha: privkskgen uses targetP::alpha through trlweSymEncryptZero(targetkey). The probe with PKS sigma256 and target sigma128 still observed RMS128.17.

Version the complete retuned fixture/evaluation profile and bind all per-level noise settings. portablelvl1param serialization and comparison currently omit alpha; the outer RAM fixture metadata also does not bind it. Source-constant changes alone cannot establish archive-noise provenance.

Regenerate affected material and validate gate, circuit-bootstrap, RAM feedback and upstream CKKS correctness at the larger noise. If sigma128 material was disclosed, rotate affected deployment secrets; stronger replacement keys do not revoke existing exposures.
The active lvl0 family becomes the weakest screened TFHE family at128.51 bits after a lvl1 sigma256 retune. Keep this in view if requiring a larger whole-system margin.
interpretation: The small0.21-bit miss should not be read as a demonstrated attack or a sharply known security level. It fails the stated strict screening policy. Likewise sigma132 passing by0.057 bits is not a convincing model-robust margin. These costs do not qualify every structured attack or operational failure probability.
